intended_object: The canonical R-algebra isomorphism R[x_k : k ≠ i][x_j⁻¹] ≅ R[X]_{(X_i X_j)}, which identifies the polynomial presentation of the overlap of the i-th and j-th standard affine charts of projective space with the degree-zero homogeneous localization. Inferred from the docstring and from how it is used later to build the chart transition maps.
explanation:
This is not a standalone mathematical notion. It is a piece of glue: a specific isomorphism that compares two presentations of the same ring, built so the library can construct its transition maps (`standardChartPolynomialTransition` and the lemmas after it).

The construction itself is correct. `StandardChartPolynomialOverlap` is `Localization.Away (X j)` in the polynomial ring in the variables other than i. `StandardChartOverlap` is shown to be `IsLocalization.Away (X_j/X_i)` over the chart. The map is obtained by sending one localization to the other along `standardChartEquiv`, which takes the variable X j to the ratio X_j/X_i, so the submonoids of powers match. It is also checked to be R-linear.

The `[Fintype ι]` hypothesis is there only because `standardChartEquiv` needs it in its proof (a surjectivity argument using finite sums and products of monomials). That is an implementation choice, and finite-dimensional projective space is the standard setting anyway. As a bundled isomorphism used for internal gluing, it has no counterpart in Mathlib and no meaningful notion of generality to judge it against.
